new Schedule(spec: ScheduleSpec | string, calendarProvider?: CalendarProvider) Parameters: Parameter Type Description spec ScheduleSpec or JSON string Schedule model. calendarProvider function or object, optional Provider for { custom: "name" } calendars. The constructor validates the schedule. Malformed JSON, invalid enum values, invalid timezone names, and structural validation failures throw. Object and JSON specs accept frequency (preferred) or the legacy freq key. Supplying both is an error, even if their values match. Serialization uses only frequency. const schedule = new Schedule({ frequency: { type: "daily", time: "09:00" }, timezone: "UTC", });

Schedules reference custom calendars with { custom: "name" }. Providers receive (name, date), where date is a YYYY-MM-DD string, and return a boolean. A function provider: const schedule = new Schedule( { frequency: { type: "daily", time: "09:00" }, timezone: "UTC", overlays: [{ calendar: { custom: "shutdown" }, rule: "exclude" }], }, (name, date) => name === "shutdown" && date === "2026-08-14", ); An object provider: const provider = { contains(name, date) { return name === "shutdown" && date === "2026-08-14"; }, }; const schedule = new Schedule(spec, provider); Without a custom provider, custom calendar dates are treated as absent from the set.

How the engine works dateme generates local recurrence times, applies calendar rules, and returns UTC instants. Separating recurrence from calendar filtering makes the rules reusable, but makeup and daylight-saving transitions need special handling. Occurrences and the series model A schedule stores a rule rather than a list of dates. An occurrence is one UTC instant produced by that rule. Queries compute the part of the series they need, including any bounds and calendar adjustments. Every query is a question about that series relative to a reference instant: next and previous find one occurrence after or before the reference instant. until and since return a window in ascending or descending order. upcoming requests a fixed number of future occurrences. Query bounds are strict: an occurrence exactly at an after or before bound is excluded. Calling next(t) with the previous result as t advances through the series without repeating it. With the same explicit anchor and a nonempty window, the first result of until(end, after) is next(after). Likewise, the first result of since(start, before) is previous(before). A schedule stores a rule rather than a list of dates. An occurrence is one UTC instant produced by that rule. Queries compute the part of the series they need, including any bounds and calendar adjustments. Every query is a question about that series relative to a reference instant: next and previous find one occurrence after or before the reference instant. until and since return a window in ascending or descending order. upcoming requests a fixed number of future occurrences. Query bounds are strict: an occurrence exactly at an after or before bound is excluded. Calling next(t) with the previous result as t advances through the series without repeating it. With the same explicit anchor and a nonempty window, the first result of until(end, after) is next(after). Likewise, the first result of since(start, before) is previous(before).

The engine first generates base occurrences from the frequency: every Monday, the first and fifteenth of each month, every third day from an anchor, or each matching cron minute. Overlays and makeup then keep, drop, or move those local dates. The engine resolves the resulting local times to UTC in the schedule’s timezone. The frequency defines when an event would occur without calendar filters. Overlays test dates independently of that recurrence, so the same holiday rule can filter a weekly, monthly, or cron schedule.

Monthly, yearly, and quarterly frequencies repeat within calendar units. every_n_days and every_n_weeks instead need an explicit start_date to fix the cycle. “Every 3 days” describes three possible series, depending on which date starts it. Cron describes matching local minutes rather than a calendar interval. It uses the same processing as other frequencies: cron generates local datetimes, then overlays and makeup adjust their dates.

Recurrence times use the schedule’s IANA timezone before conversion to UTC. “17:30 every weekday” therefore stays at 17:30 local time when daylight-saving time changes, while its UTC offset changes. A schedule with "timezone": "UTC" has no daylight-saving offset changes. In timezones with daylight-saving transitions, some local times are missing or occur twice: Spring-forward gap. Clocks jump forward, so a local time may not exist. For non-hourly frequencies, the occurrence shifts to the first valid local time after the gap. In New York, 02:30 on the spring transition date shifts to 03:00. Autumn fall-back overlap. Clocks repeat an hour, so a local time like 01:30 happens twice. The engine uses the earlier of the two instants. Hourly schedules skip nonexistent local hours. During a fall-back overlap, they emit the repeated local hour only once, at its earlier UTC instant. They follow local hour slots rather than fixed one-hour intervals in UTC.

An overlay tests an occurrence’s local date against a calendar. A 23:30 New York occurrence is checked against its New York date, which can differ from its UTC date. Top-level overlays are ANDed, so every filter must pass. An any group provides an OR condition within those filters. When an overlay drops a base occurrence, the makeup rule decides what happens: none drops the cycle. before and after search day by day, up to 14 days, for an earlier or later date that passes all overlays and destination constraints. They keep the original local time of day, subject to DST resolution. nearest searches both directions and prefers the later date on ties. Weekday maps and cascades choose a direction based on context or try fallback strategies in order. The 14-day cap prevents makeup from searching indefinitely when no nearby date passes the filters. max_makeup_hops can lower it. If the search fails, makeup_failure determines whether to skip the occurrence, keep its original date, or report an error. A selected none strategy skips it without applying the failure policy.

Makeup can change occurrence order: a later base occurrence can move before an earlier one. The engine therefore transforms a window of base occurrences and orders the results by UTC instant. until and upcoming return ascending results; since reverses them for descending order. Makeup can also create duplicates. A daily schedule that excludes a Friday holiday and makes it up on Thursday would produce two occurrences at Thursday’s scheduled time. The engine keeps one occurrence per exact UTC instant. A weekly Monday schedule moved to Tuesday has no such collision if Tuesday was not otherwise scheduled.

s: Why skip thresholds and gap checks are query rules
x: skip_if_consecutive_excluded looks at the base recurrence before makeup. It is used when a run of excluded cycles should be skipped instead of moved to nearby dates. It must run before makeup because it determines which base occurrences are eligible for adjustment. max_skip_gap checks gaps after overlays, makeup, deduplication, and bounds. It reports a query error when a checked gap exceeds the limit, without moving or adding occurrences to fill that gap.

s: Why traces are separate from ordinary queries
x: Ordinary queries return instants. Trace queries add context for callers that need to explain an occurrence in a UI or audit log, without changing the result type of ordinary queries. The reason records whether an occurrence stayed on its base date or moved from another local date, and whether DST shifted its local time. It does not record every overlay decision.

start and end limit the series to a half-open interval: no occurrence before start, none at or after end. The engine checks the final instant after makeup, so an adjustment outside the interval is dropped. Once no occurrence remains before end, next returns no result. Default iteration in Python and JavaScript requires this bound so the loop finishes. Explicit helpers such as iter_upcoming and iterBetween use a count or query window instead. Queries without an explicit window expand their search until they find enough occurrences or reach the schedule bound or absolute horizon, about 50 years from the anchor. They then return what they found. The horizon also stops searches for schedules that cannot produce an occurrence, such as a Sunday-only rule restricted to NYSE trading days with no makeup.

For a bounded query, the engine adds a local-date margin large enough for makeup on both sides of the requested window. It generates and transforms base occurrences in that wider range, orders them, and keeps only final instants inside the original query window and schedule bounds. The margin includes base dates outside the query whose makeup could move them into it. next, previous, and upcoming use the same process within an expanding window.

The engine asks a calendar provider whether a date belongs to a set. Built-in US federal and NYSE calendars use finance-dates; inline date sets and custom providers use the same filtering rules. Tests can therefore use small, fixed calendars without depending on holiday data. The WebAssembly build includes the built-in calendars, so browser schedules can use them too.

How to Skip Market Holidays and Move to the Next Open Day Exclude nyse_holiday dates and use makeup: "after" to move excluded Mondays to the next date that passes the overlay. from datetime import datetime, timezone from dateme import Schedule schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "weekly", "days": ["mon"], "time": "17:30"}, "timezone": "America/New_York", "overlays": [{"calendar": "nyse_holiday", "rule": "exclude"}], "makeup": "after", }) after = datetime(2026, 1, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc) schedule.next(after) # datetime.datetime(2026, 1, 20, 22, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc) Use "makeup": "before" to move backward. Use "makeup": "none" to drop the cycle. s: How to Run Only on Trading Days
x: Use an only overlay with nyse_trading_day to exclude weekends and market holidays. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "16:00"}, "timezone": "America/New_York", "overlays": [{"calendar": "nyse_trading_day", "rule": "only"}], "makeup": "none", })

s: How to Run on the Last Business Day of Each Month
x: Schedule the last calendar day of each month and require us_business_day. Use makeup: "before" to move back when that date is not a business day. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": { "type": "monthly_by_day", "days": [{"type": "last"}], "time": "16:00", }, "timezone": "America/New_York", "overlays": [{"calendar": "us_business_day", "rule": "only"}], "makeup": "before", })

s: How to Schedule Multiple Days in One Rule
x: List the selected weekdays in frequency.days. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": { "type": "weekly", "days": ["mon", "wed", "fri"], "time": "09:00", }, "timezone": "UTC", }) For selected weekday positions within a month, use monthly_by_weekday: schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": { "type": "monthly_by_weekday", "weekdays": [ {"nth": "first", "weekday": "tue"}, {"nth": "third", "weekday": "tue"}, ], "time": "09:00", }, "timezone": "UTC", })

s: How to Create Biweekly or Every-N-Day Schedules
x: Use every_n_weeks for a weekly cycle anchored to the week containing start_date. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": { "type": "every_n_weeks", "interval": 2, "start_date": "2026-01-05", "days": ["mon", "thu"], "time": "17:00", }, "timezone": "UTC", }) Use every_n_days for a cycle of calendar days anchored to start_date. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": { "type": "every_n_days", "interval": 3, "start_date": "2026-01-01", "time": "09:00", }, "timezone": "UTC", })

Use quarterly. month is the month within each quarter: 1, 2, or 3. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": { "type": "quarterly", "month": 1, "day": {"type": "day", "value": 15}, "time": "12:00", }, "timezone": "UTC", })

s: How to Use a Cron Expression
x: Use custom_cron for a five-field cron expression in schedule-local time. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "custom_cron", "expr": "30 9 * * 1-5"}, "timezone": "America/New_York", })

Set start, end, or both as UTC instants. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "12:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "start": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z", }) The schedule includes start and excludes end. Query bounds remain strict.

Use upcoming to request up to a fixed number of occurrences. rows = schedule.upcoming(10) Use until to list occurrences before a cutoff. from datetime import datetime, timezone end = datetime(2026, 12, 31, tzinfo=timezone.utc) rows = schedule.until(end) Use since to list past occurrences in descending order. start = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc) recent = schedule.since(start)

Use trace methods to distinguish base occurrences from makeup or DST shifts. trace = schedule.next_trace(after) if trace is not None: print(trace["instant"], trace["reason"]) For a list: rows = schedule.upcoming_trace(5, after)

s: How to Check Membership and Count a Window
x: Use is_occurrence to check a single instant and count_between to count occurrences in a strict query window. instant = datetime(2026, 1, 20, 22, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc) schedule.is_occurrence(instant) schedule.count_between(after, end) Python also supports membership syntax. instant in schedule

s: How to Iterate a Bounded Schedule
x: Set end, then iterate the schedule. Iteration uses start as an exclusive anchor, or the current time if start is absent. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "12:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-01-04T00:00:00Z", }) for instant in schedule: print(instant) Use explicit helpers for caller-provided bounds. list(schedule.iter_between(after, end)) list(schedule.iter_upcoming(3, after)) In JavaScript: for (const instant of schedule) { console.log(instant.toISOString()); } Array.from(schedule.iterBetween(after, end)); Array.from(schedule.iterUpcoming(3, after));

Combine a makeup direction with constraints on its destination dates. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "weekly", "days": ["mon"], "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [{"calendar": "us_federal_holiday", "rule": "exclude"}], "makeup": "after", "makeup_only_on": ["tue", "wed", "thu"], "makeup_within_week": True, "makeup_exclude_weekends": True, "makeup_before_next": True, })

s: How to Use Different Makeup Rules by Weekday
x: Use a weekday map for makeup to choose a direction for each excluded date’s weekday. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "weekly", "days": ["mon", "fri"], "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [{"calendar": "us_federal_holiday", "rule": "exclude"}], "makeup": { "mon": "after", "fri": "before", "default": "none", }, })

s: How to Try Fallback Makeup Strategies
x: List makeup strategies in the order to try them. End with "none" to skip the occurrence if the preceding strategies fail. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [{"calendar": "us_federal_holiday", "rule": "exclude"}], "makeup": [ {"direction": "after", "max_hops": 3}, {"direction": "before", "max_hops": 3}, "none", ], })

s: How to Fail When Makeup Cannot Find a Date
x: Set makeup_failure to "error". This example gives makeup no search days, so an excluded occurrence triggers the failure policy. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [{"calendar": {"dates": ["2026-01-02"]}, "rule": "exclude"}], "makeup": "after", "max_makeup_hops": 0, "makeup_failure": "error", }) Python queries raise and JavaScript queries throw when they encounter the failure.

s: How to Skip Runs of Consecutive Exclusions
x: Set skip_if_consecutive_excluded to skip an entire run once that many consecutive base occurrences are excluded, without attempting makeup. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [{"calendar": {"dates": ["2026-01-05", "2026-01-06"]}, "rule": "exclude"}], "makeup": "after", "skip_if_consecutive_excluded": 2, })

s: How to Alert on Long Gaps
x: Set max_skip_gap to the largest gap, in days, that queries should allow. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "weekly", "days": ["mon"], "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "max_skip_gap": 10, }) Queries fail when a checked gap exceeds the limit. See the Schedule model for which gaps each query checks.

Use dates for an inline date set, union to combine sets, and diff to subtract all later sets from the first. schedule = Schedule({ "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [ { "calendar": { "union": [ "us_federal_holiday", {"dates": ["2026-12-24"]}, {"custom": "company_shutdown"}, ] }, "rule": "exclude", } ], })

Use { "custom": "name" } in the schedule and pass a provider to the constructor. def contains(name: str, date: str) -> bool: return name == "company_shutdown" and date in {"2026-12-24", "2026-12-31"} schedule = Schedule( { "frequency": {"type": "daily", "time": "09:00"}, "timezone": "UTC", "overlays": [{"calendar": {"custom": "company_shutdown"}, "rule": "exclude"}], }, contains, ) JavaScript providers receive the same (name, date) arguments. const schedule = new Schedule(spec, (name, date) => { return name === "company_shutdown" && date === "2026-12-24"; });

s: How to Build Schedules with Typed Builders
x: Use dateme.model builders in Python. from dateme import Schedule, Weekly, Weekday, Overlay, CalendarId, OverlayRule, Makeup from dateme import model as m spec = m.Schedule( frequency=Weekly([Weekday.MON], "17:30"), timezone="America/New_York", overlays=[Overlay(CalendarId.NYSE_HOLIDAY, OverlayRule.EXCLUDE)], makeup=Makeup.AFTER, ) schedule = Schedule(spec) Use ScheduleSpec with the exported enum values in TypeScript. import { init, Schedule, Weekday, CalendarId, OverlayRule, Makeup } from "dateme"; import type { ScheduleSpec } from "dateme"; const spec: ScheduleSpec = { frequency: { type: "weekly", days: [Weekday.Mon], time: "17:30" }, timezone: "America/New_York", overlays: [{ calendar: CalendarId.NyseHoliday, rule: OverlayRule.Exclude }], makeup: Makeup.After, }; await init(); const schedule = new Schedule(spec);

s: How to Store and Reload a Schedule
x: Serialize the schedule to JSON, then pass that JSON to the constructor when reloading it. blob = schedule.to_json() again = Schedule.from_json(blob) In JavaScript: const blob = JSON.stringify(schedule); const again = new Schedule(blob);

Schedule model Schedules use the same JSON format for storage and construction in every binding. Recurrence times are local wall-clock times in the schedule’s timezone, with seconds and nanoseconds set to zero. start and end are UTC instants. Typed alternatives to JSON are dateme.model dataclasses in Python and the ScheduleSpec type in JavaScript/TypeScript. Schedule object Field Type Required Default Description frequency Frequency yes — The base recurrence; freq is a legacy input alias. timezone string (IANA name) yes — Timezone occurrences are generated in, e.g. "America/New_York". overlays array of Overlay no [] Calendar filters, ANDed. Empty means no filtering. makeup Makeup no "none" What to do when an overlay drops an occurrence. max_makeup_hops integer or null no null Maximum days to scan for makeup; null uses the built-in limit. makeup_failure Makeup failure no "skip" What to do when makeup cannot find an allowed destination. makeup_only_on array of weekdays or null no null Allowed makeup destination weekdays. makeup_within_week boolean no false Keep makeup within the original ISO week. makeup_exclude_weekends boolean no false Reject Saturday/Sunday makeup destinations. ma

Field Type Required Default Description frequency Frequency yes — The base recurrence; freq is a legacy input alias. timezone string (IANA name) yes — Timezone occurrences are generated in, e.g. "America/New_York". overlays array of Overlay no [] Calendar filters, ANDed. Empty means no filtering. makeup Makeup no "none" What to do when an overlay drops an occurrence. max_makeup_hops integer or null no null Maximum days to scan for makeup; null uses the built-in limit. makeup_failure Makeup failure no "skip" What to do when makeup cannot find an allowed destination. makeup_only_on array of weekdays or null no null Allowed makeup destination weekdays. makeup_within_week boolean no false Keep makeup within the original ISO week. makeup_exclude_weekends boolean no false Reject Saturday/Sunday makeup destinations. makeup_before_next boolean no false Reject makeup on or across adjacent base occurrences. skip_if_consecutive_excluded integer or null no null Skip excluded base-occurrence runs at or above this length. max_skip_gap integer or null no null Error if a query window has a gap longer than this many days. start RFC 3339 datetime or null no null No occurrence before this instant. en

JSON/native schedule constructors accept frequency (preferred) or freq (legacy), but reject both together, even if the values match. Serialization outputs only frequency. Python model schedules prefer model.Schedule(frequency=..., timezone=...) and .frequency. The freq=... keyword and .freq attribute remain supported. TypeScript ScheduleSpec accepts exactly one of frequency or freq. Rust’s public struct field remains Schedule::freq for source compatibility; its JSON representation uses frequency.
A tagged object whose type field selects the recurrence variant. The remaining fields depend on that variant.
One occurrence every hour, at minute past the hour, in local time. Field Type Description type "hourly" minute integer 0–59 Minutes past each hour. { "type": "hourly", "minute": 30 }
One occurrence per local calendar day at time. Field Type Description type "daily" time string "HH:MM" Time of day. { "type": "daily", "time": "09:00" }

One occurrence at time on each listed weekday. Field Type Description type "weekly" days array of weekday strings Non-empty; "mon"…"sun". Deduped. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. { "type": "weekly", "days": ["mon", "wed", "fri"], "time": "17:00" }

One occurrence at time for each listed MonthDay in each month. Field Type Description type "monthly_by_day" days array of MonthDay Non-empty. Deduped. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. A fixed day that does not exist in a month, such as February 31, is skipped for that month. It is not clamped to an earlier day. { "type": "monthly_by_day", "days": [ { "type": "day", "value": 1 }, { "type": "last" } ], "time": "12:00" }

One occurrence at time for each listed NthWeekday in each month. Field Type Description type "monthly_by_weekday" weekdays array of NthWeekday Non-empty. Deduped. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. An nth weekday that does not exist in a month, such as a fifth Friday in a month with four Fridays, is skipped for that month. { "type": "monthly_by_weekday", "weekdays": [ { "nth": "first", "weekday": "tue" } ], "time": "09:00" }

One occurrence per year: the MonthDay day within month, at time. A nonexistent day is skipped for that year. Field Type Description type "yearly" month integer 1–12 Month of the year. day MonthDay Day within month. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. { "type": "yearly", "month": 7, "day": { "type": "day", "value": 4 }, "time": "12:00" }

One occurrence every interval days, anchored to start_date, at time. Field Type Description type "every_n_days" interval integer >= 1 Number of days per step. start_date date string Anchor date, YYYY-MM-DD. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. { "type": "every_n_days", "interval": 3, "start_date": "2026-01-01", "time": "09:00" }

One occurrence on each selected weekday every interval weeks. The repeating week cycle is anchored to the week containing start_date. Field Type Description type "every_n_weeks" interval integer >= 1 Number of weeks per step. start_date date string Anchor date, YYYY-MM-DD. days array of weekday strings Non-empty; "mon"…"sun". Deduped. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. { "type": "every_n_weeks", "interval": 2, "start_date": "2026-01-05", "days": ["mon", "thu"], "time": "17:00" }

One occurrence every quarter, at time, using month as the month within each quarter. month: 1 means Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, 2 means Feb/May/Aug/Nov, and 3 means Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec. A nonexistent MonthDay is skipped for that quarter. Field Type Description type "quarterly" month integer 1-3 Month within each quarter. day MonthDay Day within the quarter month. time string "HH:MM" Time of day. { "type": "quarterly", "month": 1, "day": { "type": "day", "value": 15 }, "time": "12:00" }

One occurrence for every local minute matching a five-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. Field Type Description type "custom_cron" expr string Five cron fields. Fields support *, comma lists, ranges, and step syntax such as */15 or 1-5/2. Day-of-week accepts 0–7, where 0 and 7 both mean Sunday. When both day-of-month and day-of-week are constrained, both must match. { "type": "custom_cron", "expr": "30 9 * * 1-5" }
A tagged object identifying a day within a month. Form Meaning { "type": "day", "value": N } The Nth calendar day, N = 1–31. { "type": "last" } The last calendar day of the month.
An ordinal weekday within a month. Field Type Description nth Nth Which occurrence in the month. weekday weekday string "mon"…"sun".
One of: "first", "second", "third", "fourth", "fifth", "last".

An overlay filters occurrences against a calendar or a group of overlays. It tests the occurrence’s local date in the schedule’s timezone, not its UTC date. Top-level overlays are ANDed: an occurrence is kept only if it passes every overlay. Calendar overlay fields: Field Type Description calendar Calendar Which calendar set. rule "exclude" or "only" How to apply it. makeup Makeup Optional makeup override when this overlay drops date. Rule Effect exclude Drop the occurrence if its local date is in the calendar. only Drop the occurrence if its local date is not in the calendar. For example, {"calendar": "nyse_holiday", "rule": "exclude"} skips NYSE holidays; {"calendar": "nyse_trading_day", "rule": "only"} keeps only NYSE session days (also removing weekends). Use any to create an OR group. The group passes when any child overlay passes. { "any": [ { "calendar": "us_federal_holiday", "rule": "exclude" }, { "calendar": "nyse_holiday", "rule": "exclude" } ], "makeup": "none" } When a date is dropped, the engine uses the first failing top-level overlay’s makeup override, falling back to the schedule-level makeup if that overlay has none. For a failing any group, the group’s override ta

The calendar field accepts built-in identifiers or inline calendar specs. Built-in calendars are backed by the finance-dates dataset. Identifier Date set us_federal_holiday Observed US federal holidays. us_business_day Weekdays that are not US federal holidays. nyse_holiday NYSE full-day market closures. nyse_trading_day NYSE session days (a weekday that is not an NYSE holiday). An early-close day still counts as a trading day. Inline date sets: { "dates": ["2026-07-03", "2026-07-04", "2026-12-25"] } Calendar set algebra: { "union": ["nyse_holiday", "us_federal_holiday"] } { "diff": ["us_federal_holiday", "nyse_holiday"] } union contains dates present in any child calendar. diff contains dates in the first child calendar, excluding dates present in any of the remaining calendars. Children can be built-ins or nested calendar specs. Custom provider calendars: { "custom": "company_shutdown" } Python and JavaScript constructors accept an optional provider used to resolve custom calendars at query time. Missing custom calendars are treated as not in the set.

Makeup determines what happens when an overlay drops a base occurrence. A single direction applies to every excluded date: Value Effect "none" Skip the cycle entirely. "before" Move to the nearest earlier day that passes all overlays, at the same time. "after" Move to the nearest later day that passes all overlays, at the same time. "nearest" Move to the nearest day that passes all overlays, preferring later dates on ties. A weekday map selects a direction by the excluded date’s weekday: { "mon": "after", "fri": "before", "default": "none" } Weekday keys are optional. If an excluded date’s weekday is not present, the engine uses default; if default is absent, the occurrence is skipped. A cascade specifies fallback strategies: [ { "direction": "after", "max_hops": 3 }, { "direction": "before", "max_hops": 3 }, "none" ] Steps are tried in order until one finds a destination or disables makeup. A step can be a direction string or an object with direction and optional max_hops. The makeup search scans at most 14 days in each permitted direction. max_makeup_hops can lower that limit: null or an absent field uses 14 days, 0 prevents any search, and a positive integer is capped at 14. A z

The failure policy applies when an enabled makeup strategy cannot find an allowed destination within its search limit. It includes "before", "after", "nearest", weekday-selected directions, and exhausted cascades. One of: Value Effect "skip" Drop the occurrence silently. "keep_original" Emit the occurrence on its original excluded day. "error" Raise/throw from fallible queries and Python/JS methods. When the selected direction is "none", including a cascade step, the cycle is skipped and makeup_failure is ignored.

Set skip_if_consecutive_excluded to skip runs of excluded base occurrences before makeup is applied. { "skip_if_consecutive_excluded": 2 } The value is a positive integer. null or an absent field disables the rule. A run is counted over consecutive entries in the base recurrence series. When a run length is at least the threshold, every excluded base occurrence in that run is dropped and does not use makeup or makeup_failure. Set max_skip_gap to make queries fail if the returned occurrence stream has a gap longer than the configured number of days. { "max_skip_gap": 5 } until and since check the complete query window. next, previous, and upcoming check the gap from the anchor through returned occurrences, but do not treat the open search horizon after the last returned occurrence as a gap.

The recurrence key is always frequency, even when input used freq. timezone is the IANA name string ("UTC", "America/New_York", …). time is "HH:MM" (24-hour). Seconds are always zero. Weekdays are the lowercase three-letter strings "mon"…"sun". start and end are RFC 3339 datetimes, or null. Enum-valued fields (type, rule, nth, makeup, weekday makeup values, makeup_failure, calendar) use the lowercase snake_case spellings shown above. skip_if_consecutive_excluded must be null, absent, or an integer at least 1. max_skip_gap must be null, absent, or an integer at least 1. makeup_only_on must be null, absent, or an array of weekday strings. every_n_days.interval and every_n_weeks.interval must be at least 1. quarterly.month must be 1, 2, or 3. custom_cron.expr must be a valid five-field expression. union and diff calendar groups must have at least one child calendar. custom calendar names must be non-empty strings.

validate checks the schedule’s structure and raises/throws on: Condition Message hourly.minute outside 0–59 minute out of range Empty days / weekdays selection selection is empty A MonthDay value outside 1–31 month day out of range yearly.month outside 1–12 month out of range every_n_days / every_n_weeks interval below 1 interval out of range quarterly.month outside 1–3 quarter month out of range Invalid five-field cron expression invalid cron expression skip_if_consecutive_excluded less than 1 skip threshold out of range max_skip_gap less than 1 max skip gap out of range Empty overlay any group overlay group is empty Empty union / diff calendar group calendar group is empty Empty custom calendar name custom calendar name empty start not strictly before end (when both set) start must be before end Duplicate entries in days / weekdays are removed rather than rejected.

Getting started Build a schedule for every Monday at 17:30 New York time, moving NYSE holidays to the next date that passes the calendar filter. Then query its next, previous, and upcoming occurrences using fixed dates so the results are repeatable. Before you start Install the package: pip install dateme Open a Python session and import Schedule and the datetime types: from datetime import datetime, timezone from dateme import Schedule Step 1 — Describe the schedule Create a schedule from this JSON: spec = """ { "frequency": { "type": "weekly", "days": ["mon"], "time": "17:30" }, "timezone": "America/New_York", "overlays": [ { "calendar": "nyse_holiday", "rule": "exclude" } ], "makeup": "after", "start": null, "end": null } """ schedule = Schedule.from_json(spec) The frequency sets Monday at 17:30 in America/New_York. The overlay excludes NYSE holidays, and makeup: "after" moves each excluded occurrence to the next date that passes the overlay. Step 2 — Check it is valid The constructor validates the schedule. Call validate() to check it again; it returns without output when the schedule is valid: schedule.validate() Step 3 — Ask when it next fires Ask for the first occurrence aft
Install the package: pip install dateme Open a Python session and import Schedule and the datetime types: from datetime import datetime, timezone from dateme import Schedule

Create a schedule from this JSON: spec = """ { "frequency": { "type": "weekly", "days": ["mon"], "time": "17:30" }, "timezone": "America/New_York", "overlays": [ { "calendar": "nyse_holiday", "rule": "exclude" } ], "makeup": "after", "start": null, "end": null } """ schedule = Schedule.from_json(spec) The frequency sets Monday at 17:30 in America/New_York. The overlay excludes NYSE holidays, and makeup: "after" moves each excluded occurrence to the next date that passes the overlay.
The constructor validates the schedule. Call validate() to check it again; it returns without output when the schedule is valid: schedule.validate()

s: Step 3 — Ask when it next fires
x: Ask for the first occurrence after January 13, 2026: after = datetime(2026, 1, 13, tzinfo=timezone.utc) schedule.next(after) You should see: datetime.datetime(2026, 1, 20, 22, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc) January 19 is Martin Luther King Jr. Day, when the NYSE is closed. The overlay excludes that Monday, and makeup moves it to Tuesday, January 20 at 17:30 New York time. The returned instant is 22:30Z, five hours ahead of New York in January.

Request the next three occurrences from the same reference instant: schedule.upcoming(3, after) [datetime.datetime(2026, 1, 20, 22, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc), datetime.datetime(2026, 1, 26, 22, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc), datetime.datetime(2026, 2, 2, 22, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)] The first is the Tuesday makeup occurrence; the other two are Mondays.

Use previous to find the last occurrence before the same reference instant: schedule.previous(after) datetime.datetime(2026, 1, 12, 22, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc) The result is Monday, January 12 at 17:30 New York time.

Use until to list occurrences between two instants in ascending order: end = datetime(2026, 2, 15, tzinfo=timezone.utc) for occurrence in schedule.until(end, after): print(occurrence) 2026-01-20 22:30:00+00:00 2026-01-26 22:30:00+00:00 2026-02-02 22:30:00+00:00 2026-02-09 22:30:00+00:00

The schedule uses a market-holiday filter and makeup rule to produce UTC instants. You queried it with next, previous, upcoming, and until. For the same window in descending order, use since(after, end). Next steps: For scheduling recipes, see the How-to guides. For every field you can put in a schedule, see the Schedule model. For recurrence generation and calendar behavior, read How the engine works. To use the same schedule in the browser, see the JavaScript API.
